endorsements.quote: Net documentation minutes saved per scheduled hour, minus verification time spent on AI-generated outputs, reported separately from changes in cognitive task load
Workforce impact assessment before and after deployment; staffing adjustments funded before throughput expansion

unlisted_practices: Governance should preassign a defined share of AI-reclaimed clinician capacity to nonvisit care such as follow-up, continuity, and safety-netting.
Health systems should protect same-team continuity slots in scheduling templates and track continuity indices against pre-implementation baselines.
Health systems should run regular panel-registry reviews of patients with overdue follow-up, unresolved abnormal results, or repeated missed appointments, with protected clinician time to act.
Payers and purchasers should adopt hybrid and value-based payment, continuity add-on payments, and monthly per-patient care-management payments conditioned on closed-loop follow-up.
Purchasers should require contract clauses obliging health systems to report how AI-enabled capacity was allocated.
Health systems should require equity-stratified reporting of follow-up completion by language, age, multimorbidity, and area-level deprivation, and direct outreach to strata falling behind.
Vendor implementation agreements should require standardized reporting of time use, verification burden, and cognitive task load, and cap verification workload through implementation parameters.
Health systems should fix explicit pre-implementation baselines for panel size and session load and require that raising them be an explicit decision.
Health systems should include a patient-reported item on whether someone is following up on unresolved concerns in experience-of-care surveys.
Health systems should pair allocation indicators with balancing measures such as appointment wait time, unplanned acute care use, total cost per attributed patient, and workforce burden.
Health systems should define setting-specific allocation priorities and destinations before or early in each new AI deployment.
Health systems should assign named responsibility for each pending result or referral and establish standing recontact protocols for unresolved concerns.
Health systems should protect visit length and monitor cognitive task load and patient-reported attention when AI gains are primarily cognitive rather than converting them into added volume.

screen.reason: This is a health policy and governance framework/commentary paper discussing how health systems and payers should govern the clinical capacity ('attention dividend') reclaimed through ambient AI documentation.
